classification.difficultyReason: Combine vertical-opposite and straight-angle relationships, including two equal unknown sectors.

content.prompt: Determine the value of each unknown angle.

spec.description: Shallow X with central dot and four single arcs. Top 140°, left 40°, right 40°, bottom e°.
spec.mathematics: Both 40° givens are retained; the top and bottom angles are vertically opposite.

spec.description: X with central dot, four arcs, top and bottom 115°, right 65° and left u°.
spec.mathematics: Both 115° givens are retained. u is opposite 65°.

spec.description: Horizontal line intersects a near-vertical line leaning down-right. Central dot and four arcs; upper-left u°, upper-right and lower-left 97.25°, lower-right 82.75°.
spec.mathematics: Both 97.25° givens and two decimal places are preserved. u is vertically opposite 82.75°.

spec.description: Two oblique straight lines, central dot and four arcs. Top k°, right 117°, bottom 63°, left t°.
spec.mathematics: k is opposite 63°; t is opposite 117°.

spec.description: Horizontal and near-vertical straight lines meet at a filled dot. An extra northwest ray splits the upper-left sector into 33° and 48°. Lower-right g° has its own arc.
spec.mathematics: Upper-left components total 81° and are vertically opposite g. Ray directions are 0°, 99°, 147°, 180° and 279°.
spec.answerVisibility: 33° and 48° are givens; g° remains unknown.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}33+48&=g\\81&=g\end{align*}$$
Therefore $g=81^\circ$.

spec.description: Northwest–southeast line intersects a gently descending line. A heavier southwest ray divides the lower obtuse angle into two sectors labelled x°. Central dot, one upper arc and two lower arc portions.
spec.mathematics: The upper 150° sector is vertically opposite the two x° sectors together. No equal-angle ticks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: 150° is given; both x° labels remain unknown.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}x+x&=150\\2x&=150\\x&=75\end{align*}$$
Each unknown angle is $75^\circ$.
